001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
006
007/**
008 * A press or release of the pump's button, with a millisecond timestamp. Seen on the t:slim X2 and
009 * the Tandem Mobi.
010 *
011 * <p>Tandem's export and its Mobi app do not name this opcode, so the class name and the button
012 * interpretation are provisional. The layout is well supported: uint32 {@code timeOfDayMs} at
013 * bytes 10-13, {@code state} at byte 14, zeros at 15-25 (1772/1772 records from at least 8 pumps,
014 * X2 and Mobi).
015 *
016 * <p>The button reading rests on three observations. On the Mobi, where tubing is filled by holding
017 * the pump button, every tubing-prime start ({@link PrimeInprocessHistoryLog}) was immediately
018 * preceded by one of these with state 1 (113/113 on 4 pumps). A triple press (1, 0, 1, 0, 1 within
019 * 0.6 s) was immediately followed by a {@link SnoozeActivatedHistoryLog} in the same second. On the
020 * X2, whose button wakes the screen, press/release pairs typically last about 0.2 s.
021 * See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/148.
022 */
023
024/**
025 * History log record Pump Button, opCode 17, size 26.
026 *
027 * <br>
028 *
029 * A press or release of the pump's button, with a millisecond timestamp. Seen on the t:slim X2 and
030 * the Tandem Mobi.
031 *
032 * <p>Tandem's export and its Mobi app do not name this opcode, so the class name and the button
033 * interpretation are provisional. The layout is well supported: uint32 {@code timeOfDayMs} at
034 * bytes 10-13, {@code state} at byte 14, zeros at 15-25 (1772/1772 records from at least 8 pumps,
035 * X2 and Mobi).
036 *
037 * <p>The button reading rests on three observations. On the Mobi, where tubing is filled by holding
038 * the pump button, every tubing-prime start ({@link PrimeInprocessHistoryLog}) was immediately
039 * preceded by one of these with state 1 (113/113 on 4 pumps). A triple press (1, 0, 1, 0, 1 within
040 * 0.6 s) was immediately followed by a {@link SnoozeActivatedHistoryLog} in the same second. On the
041 * X2, whose button wakes the screen, press/release pairs typically last about 0.2 s.
042 * See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/148.
043 *
044 * 
045 * <table border='1'>
046 * <caption>Message properties:</caption>
047 * <tr><th>&nbsp;<code>opCode</code>&nbsp;</th><td>&nbsp;<code>17</code>&nbsp;</td></tr>
048 * <tr><th>&nbsp;<code>displayName</code>&nbsp;</th><td>&nbsp;<code>"Pump Button"</code>&nbsp;</td></tr>
049 * <tr><th>&nbsp;<code>internalName</code>&nbsp;</th><td>&nbsp;<code>""</code>&nbsp;</td></tr>
050 * </table>
051 */@HistoryLogProps(
052    opCode = 17,
053    displayName = "Pump Button",
054    internalName = ""
055)
056public class PumpButtonHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
057
058    private long timeOfDayMs;
059    private int state;
060
061    public PumpButtonHistoryLog() {}
062    public PumpButtonHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, long timeOfDayMs, int state) {
063        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
064        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, timeOfDayMs, state);
065        this.timeOfDayMs = timeOfDayMs;
066        this.state = state;
067    }
068
069    public int typeId() {
070        return 17;
071    }
072
073    /**
074     * <table border="1">
075     * <caption>Parsed fields for PumpButtonHistoryLog:</caption>
076     * <tr><td><code>timeOfDayMs</code></td><td><code>Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10)</code></td></tr>
077     * <tr><td><code>state</code></td><td><code>raw[14] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
078     * </table>
079     */
080    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
081        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
082        this.cargo = raw;
083        parseBase(raw);
084        this.timeOfDayMs = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10);
085        this.state = raw[14] & 0xFF;
086    }
087
088    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, long timeOfDayMs, int state) {
089        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
090            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(17, 0),
091            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
092            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
093            Bytes.toUint32(timeOfDayMs),
094            new byte[]{ (byte) state }));
095    }
096
097    /**
098     * Milliseconds since midnight on the pump's local clock, the same clock as
099     * {@link #getPumpTimeSec()}: {@code timeOfDayMs / 1000 == pumpTimeSec % 86400} in 1772/1772
100     * records. It gives sub-second ordering within the record's second; it is not a motor or
101     * encoder count.
102     */
103    public long getTimeOfDayMs() {
104        return timeOfDayMs;
105    }
106
107    /**
108     * Byte 14: 1 or 0, alternating (880 records with 1, 892 with 0). Read as 1 = pressed,
109     * 0 = released; see the class comment for why that reading is provisional.
110     */
111    public int getState() {
112        return state;
113    }
114
115    public boolean isPressed() {
116        return state == 1;
117    }
118}
